name: 努尔
src: 山铜纪/山铜纪时段_五_七城的年月.md:370
who: Nur of the Emberhorn clan, a fire-horn demon-kin girl of the old camp on the lava plain below the Horn City, ten years old in 742 and looking exactly ten, a small child and NOT a teenager: about 132 cm, thin, a fast runner who climbs walls without a ladder, wholly covered by her clothes. Skin of the reddish fire-horn hue that glows like coals at a furnace mouth when she has been running. Always barefoot, the soles of her feet as hard as the black ground of the lava plain. A pair of new horns just sprouted, a finger long, pale in colour and warm to the touch. Glossy black hair tied back loosely with a red cord that comes undone after a few steps. Dark gold eyes that look at your horns first. A blunt, stubborn, literal-minded air.
palette: ember red and glossy black, dark gold, faded brown wool, a little cord red
casual: Her everyday clothes: an old brown wool coat her elder brother outgrew, far too big for her, the sleeves rolled up three times, buttoned over a long-sleeved coarse tunic that reaches below the knees, wide trousers rolled at the shin, bare feet as all the lava-plain children go; at her waist a small leather pouch of black stones picked up by the old camp's fire. She holds one of the black stones in her palm, a direct, curious look.
private: Back by her grandmother's fire in the old camp: a long-sleeved undyed wool tunic to the shins, a knitted shawl round her shoulders, bare feet, the black hair loose and the red cord tied round her wrist. She holds a small clay cup of warm milk in both hands. A sleepy, contented look.
battle: On the west wall of the Horn City on the day of the seven bends, calling out where the fire is: the outgrown coat buttoned up to the collar, the sleeves rolled, bare feet on the warm stone, the red cord tied tight for once. One hand is cupped beside her mouth as she calls and the other points down the slope; she does not fight.
battle_pose: 3) the wall-top outfit: alert and stubborn, the feet planted on the stone, a fierce little frown, one hand cupped beside her mouth as she calls out and the other pointing down and to one side; she does not fight.
formal: On the day the names are read at the Horn City's gate: the old coat brushed clean and buttoned to the collar over a fresh undyed tunic, a new red cord in her hair, still barefoot. She stands very straight with the hands clasped in front, a solemn little face.
art: A head-and-shoulders portrait, the face turned slightly, the dark gold eyes looking at the viewer seriously, as if checking whether you have horns, the little new horns catching a warm light. Hot orange light rising from a crack of lava on one side against blue dusk. Foreground blur: drifting embers, a loosened red cord and the edge of a warm black stone. She wears the outgrown brown coat buttoned to the collar.

name: 涅芙拉
src: 山铜纪/山铜纪时段_五_七城的年月.md:1728
who: Nefra, called Dreammirror, a demon-kin of the nightmare bloodline and the youngest daughter of the Mirror Hall house, who went down forty-nine layers of nightmare to lead eleven hundred and three children back to their beds and came back without her own birth name; a hundred and seventy in 803 and looking about thirty: small and slight, about 156 cm, so light on her feet that they seem to hover a finger above the ground. Very long deep violet hair whose tips drift away like star-dust. Short pointed ears. Violet eyes with a new sheen like the surface of a black lake, in which whoever meets them sees their own dream. A folded note always tucked into one cuff. She carries nothing that reflects. A gentle, careful, few-worded air.
build: 156 cm, small and slight: a small bust, a very narrow waist and slim hips.
palette: deep grey and deep violet, star-dust lilac, dull tin, deep teal
casual: Her everyday wear in the mirror city: the old deep grey long coat, its hem mended many times, a folded note tucked into one cuff, over a plain deep teal long-sleeved dress of the mirror-city cut with the cuffs tied close, soft dark shoes; at her waist a small cloth bag holding a chipped copper coin and a dented tin cup. Nothing she wears shines or reflects. Her hands are loosely folded, a soft, distant look.
private: In the little room behind the mirror hall in the morning, going over yesterday with the first pupil who comes: a soft dark grey knitted dress, a light shawl, the long hair loose. She holds the dented tin cup of water she drinks only once the day before has been checked. A quiet, small smile.
battle: Going down into a sleeper's dream at the bedside: the deep grey coat belted close, the folded note in her cuff, the cloth bag at her waist. One hand is raised with a faint glitter of sleep-sand at the fingertips, the other holds the dented tin cup; she carries no weapon.
battle_pose: 3) the dream-walking outfit: calm and intent, the feet light and close together, a still, focused expression, one hand raised with two fingertips together as if about to touch a sleeper's brow, a faint glitter of sleep-sand on them, the other holding the dented tin cup; she carries no weapon.
formal: At the night class of the mirror hall: the deep teal long robe the hall made for her, its cuffs and collar fitted close, long sleeves, a narrow dark sash, nothing reflective, star-dust drifting from the tips of her hair. She stands with the hands together at her waist, a gentle, serene look.
art: A portrait with the camera tilted, the face large, the violet eyes deep and still like a black lake with a faint glimmer of someone else's dream in them, star-dust drifting from the tips of her hair. Warm low lamplight at a bedside from one side against the cold violet of night. Foreground blur: a lit bedside lamp, a dented tin cup and drifting star-dust. She wears the old deep grey coat.

name: 埃斯本
src: 山铜纪/山铜纪时段_五_七城的年月.md:1784
who: Esben Mirrorgrind, a demon-kin of the nightmare bloodline, of the shadow-walker kind, who married into the mirror-grinders' family by the black lake of the mirror city and grinds obsidian mirrors in their lakeside workshop; a hundred and thirteen in 803 and looking about thirty: about 181 cm, tall and thin, the shoulders bent a little forward from years of bowing over the grinding stone, the arms long. Short ink-blue hair. Pale lilac eyes; deep lines fan out at their corners when he smiles. Both palms are rubbed so smooth by the stone that they catch the lamplight, and there is always black obsidian dust on his fingers. A small copper lamp hangs at his belt. A patient, plain, few-worded air; he would rather guard a lamp all night than talk.
build: 181 cm, tall and thin: the shoulders bent a little forward, long arms.
palette: ink blue and pale lilac, obsidian black, sun-bleached leather, warm copper lamplight
casual: His workshop clothes: a leather apron worn almost white, its pockets heavy with small grinding stones, over a long-sleeved dark grey-teal wool shirt with the cuffs tied close in the mirror-city way, dark trousers and soft shoes; a small copper oil lamp hangs on a hook at his belt. He holds a palm-sized disc of black obsidian he is grinding, a quiet, patient half-smile.
private: At home in the lakeside workshop at night: a loose undyed linen shirt with the sleeves rolled up, a dark knitted waistcoat, dark trousers and soft house shoes, the apron hung up. He holds his lit copper lamp in both hands with the wick turned low, for he has slept with a lamp burning ever since those seven nights. A tired, gentle look.
battle: Keeping the lamp for someone who has gone down into a dream: a thick dark grey-teal wool coat buttoned to the collar under the pale leather apron, a wool scarf, soft shoes that make no sound. He holds the lit copper lamp up before his chest in both hands; he never goes into the dream himself and carries no weapon.
battle_pose: 3) the lamp-keeping outfit: braced and unmoving, the feet planted, a set, steady expression, holding the lit copper lamp up before his chest in both hands; he carries no weapon.
formal: On the morning his family carves his daughter's name at the city gate, dressed no finer than he ever will: his work clothes washed and brushed, a clean dark grey-teal wool coat of the mirror-city cut with a high collar and close cuffs, the old apron scrubbed pale and still tied on over it, the copper lamp polished at his belt. He stands very straight with the hands folded in front, a quiet, moved look.
art: A portrait with the camera tilted, the face large, the pale lilac eyes lowered to a disc of black obsidian in his hands, its polished face catching a warm flicker of lamplight, deep lines at the corners of his eyes. A small copper oil lamp burns low on one side, warm amber against the cold blue mist of a lake at night. Foreground blur: drifting black obsidian dust, the glowing wick of the lamp and the dark edge of a polished mirror. He wears the pale leather apron over the dark grey-teal shirt.

name: 萝塔
src: 山铜纪/山铜纪时段_五_七城的年月.md:1840
who: Lotta Mirrorgrind, a demon-kin girl of the nightmare bloodline, a dream-singer, the daughter of the mirror-grinders' family by the black lake of the mirror city, nine years old in 803 and looking exactly nine, a small child and NOT a teenager: about 128 cm, thin and long-legged, quick on her bare feet, wholly covered by her clothes. Cherry-pink hair in two thick braids, one tied with a length of rough hemp cord from the workshop. Pale lilac eyes like her father's. One front tooth missing, so the gap shows when she grins. She sings everything off-key and beats time with both hands, off the beat too. A lively, stubborn, question-asking air.
palette: cherry pink and pale lilac, oatmeal wool, hemp beige, a little dark teal
casual: Her everyday clothes: a hand-knitted oatmeal wool shawl one size too big, knitted by her mother, wrapped over a long-sleeved dark teal wool dress to the shins with the cuffs tied close, thick knitted stockings and soft little shoes; one braid tied with a piece of hemp cord from the mirror workshop. She holds a pebble she has been drawing with, a wide gap-toothed grin.
private: At home by the fire at bedtime: a long soft cream nightgown with long sleeves and a high round neck, the big knitted shawl round her shoulders, thick socks, the braids loosened. She holds a slice of honey bread in both hands. A sleepy, happy look.
battle: The five days she sat by a sleeper's bed and sang the way up: the knitted shawl pulled tight over the long dark teal dress, the cuffs tied, thick stockings, bare feet. She holds a small cup of water in one hand and beats time in the air with the other, singing; she has nothing to fight with.
battle_pose: 3) the singing outfit: steady and determined, the feet planted, a stubborn little frown, the mouth open in song, one hand beating time in the air and the other holding a small cup of water; she does not fight.
formal: At the night class of the mirror hall, where she is the youngest pupil: a clean long dark teal wool dress of the mirror-hall cut with the collar and cuffs fitted close, a small dark sash, the braids freshly tied with new hemp cord. She stands very straight with the hands clasped in front, trying hard to look solemn.
art: A head-and-shoulders portrait, the face turned slightly, the pale lilac eyes looking at the viewer with a bright gap-toothed grin, one small hand raised beside her cheek beating time to an off-key song. Warm lamplight from one side against the cool blue mist of a lake at night. Foreground blur: drifting motes of light, the hemp-tied end of a braid and the edge of a knitted shawl. She wears the big oatmeal knitted shawl over the dark teal dress, closed at the collar.

name: 赛勒斐恩
src: 山铜纪/山铜纪时段_五_七城的年月.md:1987
who: Selephen, a demon-kin night-wing who grew up on the doorstep of the beastfolk messengers' post in the rain city and now keeps the lamp road across the western sky, called Nightwing since the night the sky tower fell into the sea; a hundred and eighty-four in 824 and looking thirty-five or thirty-six: about 184 cm, tall and thin, broad across the back. Short deep teal-black hair blown into a ragged mess by the high wind. Sharp blue-green eyes that look straight at people. Thin pointed ears. A pair of deep teal feathered wings folded down his back like a dark cloak, an old arrow scar at the root of the left one. When they open fully, four more wings of light and wind spread outside them, dark and half-transparent like glass, the left two larger. A terse, exact, stubborn air.
build: 184 cm, tall and thin, light-boned, with a broad back.
palette: deep teal and teal-black, storm slate, pale cyan wing-light, worn brown leather, a little copper
casual: His lamp-road clothes: an old brown leather vest with two slits down the back for the wings, over a plain dark slate shirt with the sleeves rolled to the elbow; a flat leather pouch on a strap across the chest, a keepsake of an old friend; at his waist the small copper bell of the messengers' post, its clapper no longer wrapped in cloth, and beside it a short coil of thin rope; dark close-fitting trousers rolled at the shin, bare feet. The wings are folded like a cloak. One hand rests on the bell, a sharp, brisk, unsmiling look.
private: On the spire where he sleeps above the cliff: the vest unbuttoned and hanging open, his sign that he is not leaving for a while, the slate shirt, the wings folded loose, bare feet. He holds an old rolled star chart under one arm, given to him by the tower's eldest. A tired, quiet, almost boyish look.
battle: Going into the eye of the storm to drag the airships out: the leather vest buckled tight, a leather harness strapped across the chest, the thin rope coiled on one shoulder, bare feet. All six wings are half open behind him, the deep teal pair and the four of dark glass-like light and wind. He rings the small copper bell in one hand and grips a taut, thick tow rope over his shoulder with the other; he carries no weapon.
battle_pose: 3) the storm outfit: tense and ready, the shoulders squared, the feet a little wider and planted, a hard, narrow look, the six wings half open behind him, one hand raising the small copper bell and the other gripping a taut tow rope over his shoulder; he carries no weapon.
formal: As formal as he will ever be, standing by while the stonemasons cut the names into the cliff: the old leather vest brushed and oiled over a clean slate shirt buttoned to the collar, a dark teal sash at the waist, the copper bell polished, the rope coil neat, still barefoot, the wings folded tight. He stands very straight, a spare, uneasy look, as if he would rather be flying.
art: A portrait with the camera tilted, the face large, the head turned over one shoulder so the blue-green eyes cut sharply toward the viewer, a small copper bell raised near his cheek. Cold grey-blue storm light from one side, the edge of a dark glass-like wing glowing pale cyan along its ribs. Foreground blur: torn cloud, a taut rope and loose deep teal feathers. He wears the old leather vest with the flat pouch across his chest.

name: 奥萝
src: 山铜纪/山铜纪时段_五_七城的年月.md:2043
who: Auro, a demon-kin night-wing of the High-Nest families and Selephen's mother, who sews the sails in the airship hall halfway up the leaning sky tower; two hundred and nineteen in 824 and looking about fifty: about 172 cm, tall and thin, a little stooped. Deep teal hair half gone white, coiled at the back of the head and held with two bone pins. Deep teal eyes like her son's, slow to look up. A pair of deep teal wings folded so long down her back that they brush her heels; a row of feathers is missing from them, every one sewn into the corner of a sail. Thick fingers callused so hard a needle cannot pierce them. On a cord at her neck, a single old feather, her husband's. A quiet, unhurried air, like a heron with its wings folded.
face: FACE, as in the references: a lean, long woman's face of about fifty, NOT young: fine lines at the eye corners and beside the mouth; medium, gently slanted almond eyes of deep teal with a slow, steady gaze; thin straight brows; a small closed mouth. Pale clean skin with very little shading; skin shadows a soft cool tone.
build: 172 cm, tall and thin, a little stooped: narrow shoulders, a small bust, a slim waist and gently rounded hips.
palette: deep teal and silver-white, washed canvas off-white, beeswax amber, a little bone ivory
casual: Her sail-maker's clothes: a long canvas dress washed almost white, the cuffs tied tight with thin cord, two slits in the back for the wings; at her waist a leather pouch holding needles, thread, wax and a small knife; the old feather on its cord at her neck. She holds a big sail needle with a thread through it, a fold of sailcloth over one arm, a calm, slow look.
private: In her corner of the airship hall on a cold evening: a thick dark teal knitted shawl over a long grey wool dress with long sleeves, soft felt shoes, the bone pins loosened. She holds a small bowl of beeswax warming in both hands. A tired, peaceful look.
battle: Aboard the seventh airship on the night of the storm: the canvas dress belted short over dark wool leggings, a heavy oilcloth cape over the shoulders and the folded wings, the pouch of needles at her waist. She holds a roll of spare sailcloth under one arm and the big sail needle in the other hand; she carries no weapon.
battle_pose: 3) the storm outfit: braced against the wind, the feet a little wider and planted, a firm, unblinking expression, a roll of spare sailcloth under one arm and the big sail needle in the other hand; she carries no weapon.
formal: On the cliff-top the morning the names are carved: a long dark teal wool dress with a high collar and long sleeves, a pale grey shawl, the hair freshly coiled with the two bone pins, the old feather on its cord. She stands as straight as her back allows, the hands folded in front, a grave, quiet look.
art: A portrait with the camera tilted, the face large, the deep teal eyes lifting slowly to the viewer over a fold of sailcloth, a single dark teal feather between her fingers. Warm amber lamplight of the airship hall from one side against cold sky light from the open hangar. Foreground blur: billowing sailcloth, a sail needle trailing thread and drifting feathers. She wears the washed-white canvas dress with the cord-tied cuffs.

name: 图娅·雾攀
src: 山铜纪/山铜纪时段_五_七城的年月.md:2099
who: Tuya Mistclimb, a tiefling who strings the ropes of the sky-tower harbour; she cannot fly, so she has roped every cliff to the next for those without wings; thirty-four in 824: about 162 cm, short and solid, her arms thick and strong, her palms hard with rope calluses. Sky-blue hair cropped very short. A pair of short horns at the temples sweeping back, the tips wrapped in cloth so they will not fray the ropes. A long thin tail with a forked tip, usually curled round her waist, hooked over a rope when she works. Bright orange eyes under thick brows; cheeks reddened by the cliff wind; a chipped front tooth that shows when she grins. Fair skin. A quick-mouthed, quicker-handed, never-give-in air.
build: 162 cm, sturdy and strong: thick strong arms, a medium bust, a narrow waist and full hips, the tail longer than her arm.
palette: sky blue and hemp-rope beige, worn brown leather, bright orange, a little brass
casual: Her rigger's gear: a short-sleeved fitted brown leather top that leaves both arms bare, three coils of thin rope wound round her waist, a hooked rope-knife and a small bag of wooden wedges at her belt; dark trousers with two layers of leather patched over each knee; soft-soled boots with hemp nailed onto the soles. Her tail curls round her waist; she holds a rope end with a half-tied knot, a cheeky, chipped-tooth grin.
private: On the new cliff-top platform in the first spring after the fall: a loose cream linen shirt with the sleeves rolled up, the patched trousers, the soft boots, the tail swinging free. She holds a small pot of yellow paint and a brush, about to paint a walking line for those who cannot fly. A pleased, cocky look.
battle: On the ropes between the airships in the storm: the leather top under a rigger's harness hung with iron hooks, the coils of rope at her waist, leather wraps on the forearms, the tail hooked round a rope behind her. She grips the hooked rope-knife in one hand and a taut rope in the other, ready to cut a fouled line, a sharp, fierce look.
formal: As tidy as she will ever look, since she refuses anything finer: a clean sleeveless dark leather jerkin of the sky-tower cut over the cream shirt, a short grey wool cape pinned at one shoulder, new cloth wrapped on the horn tips, the knee patches freshly stitched, the soft-soled boots. She stands with the hands at her sides and the tail curled round one leg, a grudging, half-proud look.
art: A portrait with the camera tilted, the face large, leaning out sideways from a taut rope she grips overhead, the bright orange eyes grinning at the viewer, the chipped tooth showing. Bright cold sky light from one side over a cliff edge, her forked tail curled round the rope behind her. Foreground blur: taut ropes, a big hemp knot and drifting mist. She wears the short-sleeved leather top with the rope coils at her waist.

name: 格罗姆
src: 山铜纪/山铜纪时段_五_七城的年月.md:2269
who: Grom of the Anvil family, whom the west calls the Thunder-Tamer, a demon-kin of the bull-horned Thunder-Gaol folk and the locksmith who keeps the prison of the old forge camp at the edge of the storm wasteland; two hundred and fifty in 847 and looking about fifty: a colossus, about 215 cm, shoulders as wide as a city gate. Deep bronze-coloured skin, warm to the touch. Long grey-black hair in a braid at one side, a short dark beard. A pair of massive bull horns curving out to the sides, each ringed by an old iron padlock he hammered round. A broad burn scar across both shoulders. Purple branching marks like lightning climb his neck, arms, chest and back and glow faintly. Pale grey eyes that look at the door behind you before your face. A slow, quiet, gentle air.
build: about 215 cm, enormous and heavy: shoulders as wide as a gate, a huge chest and thick arms.
palette: deep bronze and dark iron, lightning purple, worn brown leather, grey-black
casual: His smith's and gaoler's clothes: a heavy blacksmith's leather apron over a sleeveless coarse undyed tunic, both arms bare, the old burn scars on them overlaid by the purple branching marks; dark trousers and heavy boots; a short-handled locksmith's hammer slung on his back; a roll of lock-wire and a bag of nails at his belt; on a leather cord at his neck an old iron key and an iron ring that clink together. His arms hang loose at his sides, a heavy, calm, patient look.
private: Sitting out the thunder season under the iron stakes, as he does every night now: the apron off, the sleeveless tunic, the purple marks on his arms glowing faintly, heavy boots. He holds a small three-legged stool he has just made, one leg a little short, as all his stools are. A quiet, gentle look.
battle: Leading the long chain into the wasteland: the leather apron belted tight over the sleeveless tunic, leather bracers, heavy boots; a heavy iron chain locked to his left wrist, its loose end coiled over the forearm, the purple marks blazing along his arms. He grips the short-handled locksmith's hammer in his right hand, a still, heavy, braced look.
formal: On a morning when the locks open by themselves at dawn: a long heavy dark brown wool coat buttoned across the chest with plain iron buttons over the sleeveless tunic, the apron left off, the padlocks on his horns polished, the old key and the iron ring on their cord outside the coat. He stands as straight as a pillar, the hands clasped before him, a grave, composed look.
art: A portrait from slightly below with the camera tilted, the face large, the head lowered so the padlock-ringed horns frame it, the pale grey eyes looking straight at the viewer, heavy and patient. Violet-white storm light from one side, the purple branching marks on his neck glowing. Foreground blur: rain, a hanging iron key with a ring and links of chain. He wears the blacksmith's leather apron over the sleeveless tunic.

name: 乌戈
src: 山铜纪/山铜纪时段_五_七城的年月.md:2326
who: Ugo, a demon-kin of the bull-horned Thunder-Gaol folk, eldest son of the Anvil family and Grom's uncle, who no longer remembers who he was after a hundred and twenty-five years turning a winch at the bottom of a pit; two hundred and ninety-five in 847, his body ageing fast since it was set free, looking about seventy: about 241 cm, very tall, gaunt and big-framed, the back stooped. His horns were sawn off flat at the roots, the stumps rubbed smooth and shiny. Close-cropped iron-grey hair; eyebrows half white; very pale grey eyes. Deep bronze-coloured skin with an ashen grey cast. A small branded mark on the collarbone; an old ring scar round one ankle. A slow, quiet, gentle air; he sits outside a new prisoner's door all night so no one spends the first night alone.
face: FACE, as in the references: a gaunt old demon-kin man's face of about seventy, long and heavy-boned, NOT young: deep-set, very pale grey eyes under eyebrows gone half white, deep lines across the brow and down the cheeks, a broad nose, a slack, quiet mouth. Deep bronze-coloured skin with an ashen grey cast and very little shading; skin shadows a soft cool brown.
build: 241 cm, very tall, gaunt and big-framed: broad bony shoulders, long arms, a stooped back.
palette: ashen bronze and iron grey, patched brown wool, dull chain iron, a little clay red
casual: His clothes: an old dark brown wool coat that Grom gave him, patched many times and short in the sleeves, over a coarse undyed shirt, wide trousers and worn boots; three loops of iron chain wound round his waist, every clasp turned outward, his brother's. He holds a plain clay bowl of water in both hands, a mild, puzzled look.
private: Outside a cell door on a quiet afternoon: the patched coat open over the coarse shirt, the chain at his waist. He holds under one arm the small stool with four equal legs that Grom made for him. A drowsy, peaceful look.
battle: On the long chain into the wasteland, last in the line: the patched coat belted, the chain loops at his waist, a short length of the great chain locked to his wrist, a big leather water-skin slung on his back. He holds out a clay bowl, about to pass water down the line; he carries no weapon.
battle_pose: 3) the march outfit: steady and patient, the feet a little wider and planted, a calm expression, a big water-skin on his back and a clay bowl held out in both hands; he carries no weapon.
formal: As neat as he ever gets, on a day the gaol's doors open: the patched coat brushed and buttoned to the collar, a clean undyed shirt, the chain loops at his waist with the clasps turned outward. He stands upright for once, the big hands hanging at his sides, a mild, slightly lost look.
art: A portrait with the camera tilted, the face large, the very pale grey eyes looking at the viewer kindly from under half-white brows, a clay bowl of water held near his chest. Dim warm lamplight from one side in a stone corridor before dawn. Foreground blur: the edge of an iron cell door, drifting dust and a loop of iron chain. He wears the old patched brown coat.

name: 舍克尔·枷匠
src: 山铜纪/山铜纪时段_五_七城的年月.md:2382
who: Shekker Shacklewright, a demon-kin troll of the Thunder-Gaol folk who grew up in the thunder vault under the storm wasteland and led its raids until he was taken and condemned; thirty-two in 847: very tall, about 232 cm, leaner than most trolls, broad-shouldered and long-armed, light-footed. Thick hide of grey with a blue-green tint. His head is shaved down to a dark stubble, for long hair stands up and draws the lightning. Pale gold eyes under half-lowered lids that lift only to watch the sky. Under the skin of both hands glows a coppery sheen, his family's blood, tinged purple from the vault. A small leather pouch of gravel hangs at his belt. A quiet, exact air; he says only what is true.
build: 232 cm, very tall and lean for a troll: broad shoulders, long arms, one foot always half a step ahead.
palette: grey with blue-green, pale gold, coppery violet glow, grey wolf fur, coarse undyed cloth
casual: The gaol's issue: a coarse undyed long-sleeved tunic and wide trousers belted with rope, the cuffs tied, worn shoes; a faint chain mark round one ankle; at his belt a small leather pouch of gravel picked from under the wasteland's waymarks. He stands at the gate with the hands loose at his sides, the coppery sheen showing on them, a level, watchful look.
private: Before the memorial stone in the early morning: the coarse tunic with the sleeves rolled up, a grey wool cloak over the shoulders. He holds one small stone from the pouch in his open palm. A quiet, heavy look.
battle: Leading the chained line through the wasteland: a short coat sewn from thunder-maned wolf pelt, worn against the lightning, over the coarse tunic, leather wraps on the shins, a length of chain locked to his ankle. He holds one hand up, palm out, signalling the line to stop, and grips a handful of gravel in the other; he carries no weapon.
battle_pose: 3) the wasteland outfit: tense and alert, one foot a little ahead, a firm expression, the eyes lifted to the sky, one hand raised palm out to halt the line and the other clutching a handful of gravel; he carries no weapon.
formal: As keeper at the gate of the Thunder Gaol: a clean dark grey wool coat of the gaol's keepers buttoned to the collar over the coarse tunic, a wide leather belt with the gravel pouch, the thunder-wolf pelt folded over one shoulder. He stands very straight with the hands at his sides, a grave, unflinching look.
art: A portrait with the camera tilted, the face large, the pale gold eyes lifted under heavy lids toward a storm above, a handful of small grey stones in his open palm, the coppery violet sheen glowing under the skin. Violet-white lightning light from one side. Foreground blur: a broken waymark stone, crackling sparks and drifting grit. He wears the thunder-wolf pelt coat.

name: 赛壬缇娅
src: 山铜纪/山铜纪时段_五_七城的年月.md:2548
who: Sirentia, a demon-kin of the deep-tide folk, daughter of the tide-lord family of the salt sea's old shore, who keeps the tide tables for the seven harbour towns of the deep blue bay; two hundred and eleven in 861 and looking twenty-five or twenty-six: about 166 cm, soft and supple, narrow-waisted and long-legged. Long deep sea-blue hair that is always wet and never dries. A crown of small thin silver fins at the temples in place of ears. Fine iridescent scales over the cheekbones and down the sides of the neck to the collarbone. Deep blue eyes that look first at what you are holding. She walks on land like someone who has only just learned. A careful, stubborn, exact air; she fears nothing more than a wrong number.
build: 166 cm, soft and supple: a medium bust, a very narrow waist and gently rounded hips, long legs.
palette: deep sea blue and dark navy, iridescent scale silver, oilcloth olive, a little beaten copper
casual: Her working dress on the bay: a deep blue short robe to the knees, its hem slit at the sides for diving, belted, over dark close-fitting leggings, soft dark sandals; at her belt a small leather pouch of salt from the old shore and beside it a spiral sea shell whose crack is bound with a band of beaten copper; a notebook and the tide tables wrapped in three layers of oilcloth tucked into the front of her robe. She holds the shell lightly in one hand, a careful, serious look.
private: On the stone steps under the fort at dawn, tasting the water: a loose sea-grey linen shirt-dress with long sleeves, a knitted shawl, the wet hair over one shoulder. She holds the copper-bound shell to her ear. A quiet, listening, faintly smiling look.
battle: Singing on the reef at the mouth of the bay: the slit deep blue robe soaked and belted tight, the salt pouch and the copper-bound shell at her belt, the oilcloth packet tucked in her robe, bare feet on wet rock. She lifts one hand palm-down over the water as if to hold back the tide, the other holding the shell, the lips parted to sing; she carries no weapon.
battle_pose: 3) the tide-singing outfit: tense and ready, the feet planted wide as if on wet rock, a firm, unflinching expression, the lips parted as if singing, one hand held out palm-down as if to hold back the water and the other holding the copper-bound shell; she carries no weapon.
formal: As tide-lord of the bay, coming up the steps from the sea: a long deep blue gown with a high collar and long sleeves, its long hem pooling at her feet like spilled water, a sheer sea-grey overdress, the copper-bound shell on a cord at her waist, the oilcloth notebook held in both hands. She stands very upright, the head slightly bowed, a grave, composed look.
art: A portrait with the camera tilted, the face large, the deep blue eyes looking at the viewer steadily and a little anxiously, as if checking a number, the wet sea-blue hair clinging to her neck and the iridescent scales on her cheekbone catching the light. Wavering light reflected off water from one side, cool teal. Foreground blur: drifting salt crystals, a blank fluttering page of a tide table and the copper-bound spiral shell. She wears the slit deep blue short robe.

name: 塔玛·岬火
src: 山铜纪/山铜纪时段_五_七城的年月.md:2605
who: Tama Capefire, a human of an old harbour family who has tended the beacon fire on top of the guildhall tower for ten years and cannot swim; thirty-two in 861, though sea wind and smoke make her look thirty-five or so: about 171 cm, tall and narrow-shouldered, with long legs and strong calves. Fire-red hair tied back with an old strip of cloth, a few front locks once singed and grown back curly. Teal-green eyes, the rims always a little red from smoke. Layer on layer of old burn scars on the backs of her hands, pine resin between the fingers. One sharp little canine shows when she grins. On a cord at her neck hangs an old imperial copper nail. A blunt, quick, stubborn air; she counts everything out loud.
build: 171 cm, tall: narrow shoulders, a small bust, a slim waist and gently rounded hips, long legs with strong calves.
palette: fire red and ember orange, teal green, smoke grey wool, a little old copper
casual: Her beacon-keeper's clothes: a thick grey wool coat with a few holes burned in the cuffs, over a dark linen shirt, dark trousers tucked into sturdy boots; a copper fire-striker and a short hatchet at her belt; a bundle of firewood tied on her back with a rope; the imperial copper nail on a cord at her neck. One hand holds the rope of the firewood bundle at her shoulder, a quick, blunt grin.
private: At home in the fort with her grandmother: a long brown wool dress with long sleeves, a knitted shawl, soft shoes, the red hair let loose. She holds a cup of hot water in both hands. A warm, sleepy look.
battle: On the tower top the night the sea rose: the grey wool coat buttoned up and belted, leather gloves, the hatchet at her belt, soaked to the knees. She holds the copper fire basin against her side with a small flame still burning in it and grips the short hatchet in the other hand; she is not a fighter.
battle_pose: 3) the storm outfit: braced and stubborn, the feet planted wide, a fierce, set expression, the copper fire basin held close against her side with its small flame and the short hatchet in the other hand; she is not a fighter.
formal: On the day the beacon-keepers' names are cut on the back of the stone: a clean long dark green wool dress with long sleeves and a high collar, a grey shawl, the red hair tied back with a new strip of cloth, the copper nail on its cord. She stands very straight with the hands folded in front, a proud, slightly awkward look.
art: A portrait with the camera tilted, the face large, the smoke-reddened teal-green eyes grinning at the viewer, the fire-red hair whipping in the sea wind. Warm firelight from a beacon on one side against cold blue night air over the sea. Foreground blur: drifting sparks, a small floating lamp bobbing on dark water and a rope-tied bundle of firewood. She wears the grey wool coat with burned cuffs.

name: 哈坎·四桨
src: 山铜纪/山铜纪时段_五_七城的年月.md:2661
who: Hakan of the Four-Oars family, a demon-kin of the deep-tide snake folk, an old fisherman of the Twin Reef harbour and master of a boat called Slow Tide; a hundred and seventy-one in 861 and looking about sixty: about 184 cm, broad-framed and stooped, with four arms, the upper pair thick for the helm and the nets, the lower pair thin for the oars; the lower left hand is missing two fingers. Faded grey-green scales cover him. Thin white hair, once sea-blue, tied back in a short tail. Yellow eyes with vertical slit pupils. Both knees are swollen, and he leans on a polished old oar handle as a cane. A wooden slip with the week's tide table hangs at his neck. A cheerful, chatty, kindly air.
face: FACE, as in the references: an old snake-folk man's face of about sixty, broad and weathered, NOT young: narrow yellow eyes with vertical slit pupils and deep laugh lines at their corners; faded grey-green scales over the brow, cheekbones and jaw; a wide, talkative mouth. Clean skin with very little shading; skin shadows a soft cool green-grey.
build: 184 cm, broad-framed and stooped, with four arms still hard with muscle and two swollen knees.
palette: faded grey-green scales, oilcloth olive-brown, faded sea blue, weathered driftwood, a little white
casual: His fisherman's clothes: a short oilcloth jacket with four armholes cut in it, over a faded sea-blue shirt, wide canvas trousers rolled at the calf and worn sea boots; a fish-gutting knife at his belt; the wooden tide slip on a cord at his neck. One hand leans on the polished oar-handle cane, another rubs a knee, the other two hold a half-mended net, a cheerful, chatty grin.
private: On the bow of his boat in the evening: a loose faded shirt with four rolled sleeves, a knitted wool cap, the wide trousers, bare feet. Two hands mend a net while the other two rub his knees. A content, sleepy look.
battle: Rowing back out into the surge for the boats behind: the oilcloth jacket belted tight, a rope coiled across the chest, the knife at his belt, sea boots. The upper hands grip a long oar held low and diagonally across his body, the lower hands hold a coil of rope; he carries no weapon but the knife.
battle_pose: 3) the surge outfit: braced and determined, the feet planted wide as on a pitching deck, a firm expression, the upper two hands gripping a long oar held low and diagonally and the lower two holding a coil of rope; he does not fight.
formal: On the day a new tide table is nailed to the fort gate: a clean dark blue wool coat with four sleeves buttoned to the collar, a faded red neckerchief, the wooden tide slip polished on its cord, the oar-handle cane in one hand. He stands as straight as his knees allow, a proud, beaming look.
art: A portrait with the camera tilted, the face large, the yellow slit-pupilled eyes crinkled in a grin at the viewer, one of his four hands slapping a swollen knee. Warm low evening light off the water from one side. Foreground blur: a fishing net, sea spray and the wooden tide slip on its cord. He wears the short oilcloth jacket with four armholes.

name: 约伦·无炉
src: 山铜纪/山铜纪时段_五_七城的年月.md:2833
who: Joren Forgeless, a dwarf of no clan from the reed-hut slums of the golden-kite capital, who keeps a great soup pot on the riverbank and gives a bowl to anyone who comes; a hundred and fifty-four in 742, looking like a human woman of about forty-five by 768: about 138 cm, short, stout and broad-shouldered. Two thick ginger-red braids coiled on top of her head, a few white hairs among them. Small bright amber eyes. A round face and a big nose with a red tip from the smoke. Thick red hands with ring on ring of burn scars on the fingers. A blunt, gruff, short-spoken air; she scolds you first and then hands you the bowl.
face: FACE, as in the references: a dwarf woman's face of about forty-five, round and ruddy, NOT a child's and with no beard: small bright amber eyes; short strong ginger brows; a big round nose with a red tip; a firm, blunt mouth. Clean skin with very little shading; skin shadows a soft warm tone.
build: 138 cm, short, stout and strong: broad shoulders, a full bust, a thick waist and full hips.
palette: ginger red and amber, oilcloth olive, iron black, river-reed beige
casual: Her riverbank clothes: an oilcloth apron with a few burned holes patched on its front, over a dark brown wool dress with the sleeves rolled to the elbow, sturdy boots; at her belt a long-handled iron ladle, a bag of salt and a kitchen knife; slung on her back the great iron soup pot, as wide as her shoulders, a line of small engraved marks round its rim, the rim below the top of her head. She raps the ladle on the pot's rim, a gruff, impatient look.
private: In her shack by the river in the evening: a loose cream linen blouse with the sleeves rolled up, a long brown skirt, the apron still on. She holds a dented pot upside down in one hand and a small mending hammer in the other, listening for the leak. A focused, grumpy look.
battle: Feeding a whole camp in a hard winter: a thick wool coat under the oilcloth apron, a wool scarf, the great pot on her back, the long-handled iron ladle gripped in one fist like a club; she is not a fighter.
battle_pose: 3) the hard-winter outfit: braced and stubborn, the feet planted wide, a fierce scowl, the great pot on her back and the long-handled iron ladle gripped in one fist like a club; she is not a fighter.
formal: At dawn on Dawn Day, after cooking all night: a clean dark brown wool dress, a freshly washed apron, the braids newly pinned on top of her head. She holds out the first bowl of the morning in both hands, kept for the empress, a stern, proud look.
art: A portrait with the camera tilted, the face large, the small amber eyes glaring at the viewer with gruff warmth, steam rising past her round face. Warm firelight from under a great pot on one side against a grey river dawn. Foreground blur: steam, the long handle of an iron ladle and drifting river reeds. She wears the oilcloth apron with the patched burn holes.

name: 桑娜
src: 山铜纪/山铜纪时段_五_七城的年月.md:2889
who: Sanna, half human and half deep-tide demon-kin, a rope-maker on the riverbank of the reed-hut slums and one of the three hundred and nineteen who lived through the night the rain city burned; a hundred and twenty in 768 and looking just over fifty: about 163 cm, thin and tall-seeming, with long fingers callused at the tips from twisting rope. Black hair with a hint of blue, streaked with white, that dries slowly and always looks freshly washed. Two thin gill slits behind her ears, hidden under a blue headscarf knotted at the back with the longhouse knot. Grey-green eyes that look at faces first. Round one wrist, a burnt remnant of rope from the old longhouse, joined with her own knot. A hard, stubborn, few-worded air.
face: FACE, as in the references: a lean woman's face of about fifty, NOT young: fine lines at the eye corners and between the brows; medium almond eyes of grey-green that look straight at your face; level dark brows; a thin, set mouth. Pale clean skin with very little shading; skin shadows a soft cool tone.
build: 163 cm, thin: a small bust, a slim waist and slim hips, long fingers.
palette: faded headscarf blue, blue-black and white, hemp beige, dark river-brown wool, grey-green
casual: Her rope-maker's clothes: an old dark brown long coat with the sleeves rolled, the hem flecked with hemp fluff, over a plain grey wool dress; the blue headscarf knotted at the back; the burnt rope round her wrist; a coil of thin cord at her belt that she twists whenever she sits. She holds a length of half-twisted rope between her hands, a hard, watchful look.
private: By her rope frame on a rainy day, the frame moved indoors: a plain long-sleeved blue-grey wool dress, a knitted shawl, the headscarf on. She holds a tiny braided wrist-cord she is knotting for a newborn of the slums. A quiet, softer look.
battle: Going into the river after a rope end swept away, or out into the lanes after a lost child: the long coat belted tight, the headscarf knotted firm, a coil of heavy rope over one shoulder; she carries no weapon.
battle_pose: 3) the river outfit: braced and alert, the feet planted, a hard, set expression, a coil of heavy rope over one shoulder and a rope end gripped in one fist; she carries no weapon.
formal: In the last row of the court's public benches: her long coat brushed clean and buttoned, a fresh blue headscarf knotted with the longhouse knot, the burnt rope on her wrist. She stands very straight with the hands folded in front, an unreadable, stubborn look.
art: A portrait with the camera tilted, the face large, the grey-green eyes studying the viewer's face, a twist of rope held between her long fingers. Grey rain light from one side over a muddy riverbank. Foreground blur: rain, a coiled hemp rope with a knot and a corner of the blue headscarf. She wears the old dark coat with the blue headscarf.

name: 卡洛塔·科赫
src: 山铜纪/山铜纪时段_五_七城的年月.md:2945
who: Carlotta Koch, a human, eldest daughter of the upper-city house that has kept the South Granary since the empress's first decrees, and the granary's clerk who has kept two sets of books for eight years; twenty-three in 767: about 166 cm, thin, holding her back perfectly straight, half a head taller than the other upper-city girls. Deep gold hair wound into a tight, hard bun. Blue-grey eyes that look at your hands before your face, to see which hand takes the money. Long thin fingers with ink always on the fingertips; when she counts, her left hand presses down on her right. A cool, exact, few-worded air; she trusts writing more than people.
build: 166 cm, thin and very upright: a small bust, a narrow waist and gently rounded hips.
palette: clerk's deep blue and black, deep gold, ink black, parchment cream, a little iron
casual: Her clerk's clothes: a deep blue clerk's coat buttoned to the very top, a pair of black cloth sleeve-guards over the cuffs against the ink, a dark skirt to the ankles and polished low boots; a ring of iron keys to the granary's back room and the account chest at her belt. She holds a ledger closed against her chest, the left hand pressing on the right, a cool, measuring look.
private: In the small room behind the court clerks' office where she lives after the trial: a plain grey wool dress with a high collar and long sleeves, the bun still tight. She holds an old long-handled iron ladle with a burn mark on its handle, her great-great-grandfather's, the one thing she kept. A quiet, thoughtful look.
battle: The night she carries the true ledger to the court: the deep blue coat buttoned to the top, the black sleeve-guards, a small shuttered lantern at her belt. She holds the thick ledger open against her forearm with the left hand pressed flat on the page; she carries no weapon.
battle_pose: 3) the reckoning outfit: tense and very upright, the shoulders squared, a firm expression, a thick ledger held open against her forearm with the left hand pressed flat on the page; she carries no weapon.
formal: At an upper-city betrothal dinner: a long high-collared gown of deep blue wool and silk with long fitted sleeves, white gloves with a small kite embroidered at the wrist in the old upper-city way, a thin gold betrothal ring worn over the glove, the bun pinned with a plain silver comb. She stands very straight with the hands folded in front, a composed, unreadable look.
art: A portrait with the camera tilted, the face large, the blue-grey eyes lifting from a page of figures to the viewer, the left hand pressing on the right over an open ledger. Cool grey morning light from a high window on one side. Foreground blur: drifting paper dust, a quill pen and a single falling bead of ink. She wears the deep blue clerk's coat with black sleeve-guards.

name: 多拉·菲舍尔
src: 山铜纪/山铜纪时段_五_七城的年月.md:3001
who: Dora Fischer, a human dock porter of the golden-kite capital who has carried sacks for thirty years and sits for the slope streets of the lower town in the new parliament; forty-seven in 767: about 172 cm, tall and strong, her shoulders as wide as a door, big hands with hard calluses. Straw-yellow hair cut short so it stays out of the way of the sacks. Bright cornflower-blue eyes. A face reddened by the dock wind, with sun freckles across the cheekbones. A loud, warm laugh you can hear half a street away. On a leather cord at her neck hangs a dented tin tag from the wall, her dead son's. A loud, blunt, warm-hearted air; she asks whether you have eaten before anything else.
face: FACE, as in the references: a broad, open woman's face of about forty-seven, NOT young: laugh lines at the eye corners; medium almond eyes of bright cornflower blue; strong brows; cheeks reddened by the wind with a scatter of freckles over the cheekbones; a wide mouth made for laughing. Clean skin with very little shading; skin shadows a soft warm tone.
build: 172 cm, tall, big and strong: shoulders as wide as a door, a very full bust, a thick waist and wide hips.
palette: canvas brown and straw yellow, cornflower blue, dull tin grey, a little dock-rope beige
casual: Her docker's clothes: an old canvas short coat with two layers of padding sewn on the shoulders, the sleeves rolled up, over a coarse linen shirt and a brown wool skirt to mid-calf, heavy boots; her son's dented tin tag on a leather cord at her neck. She stands with the fists on her hips, a loud, warm grin.
private: At home on the slope street: a faded brown wool dress with the sleeves rolled up, an apron, the tin tag on its cord. She holds out a big bowl of hot porridge, as if asking whether you have eaten. A hearty, kind look.
battle: On the gangplank, leading the porters' work song: the canvas coat with the padded shoulders, a leather back-pad strapped on, the sleeves rolled. A heavy sack of grain sits on one shoulder, steadied with one big hand, the other hand balled into a fist; she does not fight.
battle_pose: 3) the dock outfit: braced and strong, the feet planted wide, a loud, determined expression, a heavy grain sack on one shoulder steadied with one hand and the other hand balled into a fist; she does not fight.
formal: The day she stands up in the parliament: a clean deep blue wool coat buttoned to the collar, the dockside's idea of best, over a fresh linen shirt and a dark skirt, her son's tin tag still on its cord outside the coat. She stands very straight with the hands folded in front, a proud, stubborn look.
art: A portrait with the camera tilted, the face large, the cornflower-blue eyes laughing at the viewer, a dented tin tag clenched in one big fist near her chest. Warm late light off the river and the docks from one side. Foreground blur: a swinging cargo hook, hemp sacking and gulls. She wears the canvas short coat with padded shoulders.

name: 贾比尔
src: 山铜纪/山铜纪时段_五_七城的年月.md:3919
who: Jabir of the Red-Ridge clan, a fire-horn demon-kin who leads the people out of the old lava caves to break the chain of the thing they worship at the bottom of the pit; a hundred and fifty-seven in 742 and looking about forty: about 190 cm, tall and thin, a head shorter than the horned general he fights. Charcoal-grey skin with a faint red undertone. Two horns growing straight up; a blackened iron ring is locked round the root of the left horn, the mark of a blood oath. Short ash-red hair. Pale ice-blue eyes. Both arms are covered from wrist to shoulder in cut scars, new over old, from feeding beasts with his own blood. A thin obsidian blade. A cold, quiet, courteous air.
build: about 190 cm, tall and thin, long-armed.
palette: charcoal grey and ash red, rust red, blackened iron, obsidian black, lava blue
casual: His clothes from the old caves: a sleeveless scorched black leather jerkin laced up the front, leaving the scarred arms bare, a ragged rust-red sash at the waist, dark wrapped trousers and hide boots; the iron ring on his left horn; a thin obsidian blade at his side. He stands with the hands loose at his sides, a cold, courteous look.
private: In the old caves on a quiet night: a long-sleeved coarse undyed shirt hiding the scars, the rust-red sash, bare feet on warm black stone. He holds a small clay cup of water. A tired, distant look.
battle: On the black stone at the foot of the seven bends: the scorched leather jerkin, leather wraps on the forearms over the fresh cuts, the rust-red sash, hide boots. He grips the thin obsidian blade, its edge ground almost transparent, a cold, unwavering look.
formal: As head of the Red-Ridge clan at a blood-oath rite: a long dark rust-red wool robe of the plain western cut buttoned to the throat, the clan's ridge mark stitched small at the collar, a black sash, the iron ring on his horn polished. He stands very upright with the hands folded in front, a grave, cold look.
art: A portrait with the camera tilted, the face large, the pale ice-blue eyes looking at the viewer with cold courtesy, a scarred hand raised to touch the blackened iron ring on his left horn. Blue lava light from below on one side against deep shadow. Foreground blur: blue flames, drifting cinders and the thin edge of an obsidian blade.

name: 纳迪尔
src: 山铜纪/山铜纪时段_五_七城的年月.md:3936
who: Nadir of the Molten-Ring clan, a fire-horn demon-kin who once led children down into the mine pits for a demon god and is now the oldest soldier of the Army of Atonement, teaching the recruits how to carry the wounded; a hundred and eighty-two in 742 and looking about forty: about 186 cm, tall and thin. A pair of horns slanting back, a pale white mark round each tip where he smashed off the iron caps of his old trade. A scar down his left cheek. Reddish skin. Short smoke-blond hair. Dark amber eyes that always look down, at people's feet. A quiet, low-voiced air; when he is cursed, he says only yes.
face: FACE, as in the references: a lean, long man's face of about forty, quiet and weary: narrow dark amber eyes cast down, a long scar running down the left cheek, a straight nose, a closed, flat mouth. Clean reddish skin with very little shading; skin shadows a soft warm red-brown.
build: about 186 cm, tall and thin.
palette: reddish skin and smoke blond, dark amber, black iron, worn leather brown, a little bone white
casual: The Army of Atonement's plain gear: a worn black leather jerkin with iron studs nailed on the shoulders over a dark red wool shirt, dark trousers and heavy boots, a short cloak of undyed wool; a plain iron-tipped spear held low at an angle in one hand. He stands with the eyes lowered, a patient, unreadable look.
private: In the camp at night: the jerkin off, a loose dark red wool shirt with the sleeves rolled, the cloak over one shoulder. He holds a coiled carrying strap, about to show a recruit how to bear a wounded man. A quiet, steady look.
battle: On the seven bends behind the general: the black leather jerkin with iron-studded shoulders buckled tight, leather bracers, a carrying strap across the chest for bearing the wounded, heavy boots. He grips the iron-tipped spear in both hands across his body, a still, steady look.
formal: At the reading of the names at the horn city's gate: a long dark grey wool coat of the plain western cut buttoned to the collar over the red shirt, a black sash, the white-marked horn tips bare. He stands very straight with the hands folded in front, the eyes lowered, a grave look.
art: A portrait with the camera tilted, the face large, the dark amber eyes lowered past the viewer, the scar on his left cheek and the white mark on a horn tip catching the light. Hot orange lava light from one side against drifting smoke. Foreground blur: drifting ash, a carrying strap and the iron tip of a spear. He wears the black leather jerkin with iron-studded shoulders.

name: 努尔
src: 山铜纪/山铜纪时段_五_七城的年月.md:3952
who: Nur of the Emberhorn clan, a fire-horn demon-kin of the Horn City who tests the fire for its forges and, in later years, walks ahead of the Redemption Army feeling out the fire under their feet; grown up after 750, a hundred and twenty-nine by 861 and looking just over twenty: tall and thin, about 172 cm. Skin of the reddish fire-horn hue. A pair of horns grown to the length of a palm, paler in colour than other fire-horns' and warm to the touch. Glossy black hair tied firmly at the back of the head with a red cord. Dark gold eyes. Always barefoot, the soles as hard as the black ground of the lava plain. A blunt, plain-spoken air; she says everything about the fire three times.
face: FACE, as in the references: a young woman's face of about twenty, lean and direct: medium, gently slanted almond eyes of dark gold with a steady gaze; straight black brows; a small, set mouth. Clean skin of a reddish fire-horn hue with very little shading; skin shadows a soft warm red-brown.
build: about 172 cm, tall and thin.
palette: ember red and glossy black, dark gold, soot grey, a little cord red
casual: Her forge-watcher's clothes in the Horn City: a fitted soot-grey wool tunic with long sleeves, belted with a broad leather belt, a short scorched leather apron for the forge, dark close-fitting trousers rolled at the shin, bare feet; at her waist the same small leather pouch of black stones from the old camp's fire that she has carried since she was a child. She stands with the hands loose at her sides, a blunt, direct look.
private: At home in the Horn City after the forges are banked: a long-sleeved dark red wool dress to the calves, a woven shawl, bare feet, the red cord loosened. She turns one small black stone from the pouch in her fingers. A quiet, inward look.
battle: Walking ahead of the Redemption Army over the cooling lava: a short scorched leather jerkin over the soot-grey tunic, leather wraps on the forearms, the red cord tied tight, bare feet. One hand points ahead to where the fire runs, the other holds a short iron-tipped probing staff low; she carries no other weapon.
battle_pose: 3) the fire-walking outfit: alert and intent, the bare feet planted, a firm expression, one hand pointing ahead to where the fire runs and the other holding a short iron-tipped probing staff low; she carries no other weapon.
formal: At the reading of the names at the Horn City's gate: a long dark red wool coat of the plain western cut buttoned to the collar, a black sash, a fresh red cord in her hair, still barefoot. She stands very straight with the hands folded in front, a grave look.
art: A portrait with the camera tilted, the face large, the head bowed a little as if listening to the stone, the dark gold eyes lifting to the viewer, the pale horns glowing warm. Hot orange light from a forge mouth on one side against cool dawn blue. Foreground blur: drifting sparks, the end of a red cord and the rim of a small bronze bell.

name: 安布罗斯
src: 山铜纪/山铜纪时段_五_七城的年月.md:3991
who: Ambrose, a demon-kin blood-drinker of the crimson-feast folk, the blood-oath priest of the feast city, who sits on a small chair behind the first seat of the long table; about a hundred and fifty-eight in 758 and looking just over forty: about 180 cm, thin and tall. Dark green hair cropped very short. A smooth face without a single line. Vivid vermilion eyes. Long thin fingers whose tips are stained dark red from writing rites in blood. A slow, precise, prayer-like way of speaking; he says I refuse as if it were a blessing.
build: about 180 cm, thin and tall, with long thin fingers.
palette: faded crimson and dark green, dried-blood red, tarnished silver, candle ivory
casual: His priest's dress: a long faded red priest's robe with long sleeves and a high collar, its hem embroidered with the pattern of an old high seat, a dark sash, soft dark shoes; a small book of rites hanging at his belt on a cord. His red-tipped fingers are folded before him, a calm, unsettling smile.
private: In his cell behind the empty high seat at night: a plain dark long-sleeved shirt and dark trousers, the robe hung up. He holds a thin bone stylus and a slip of paper, writing. An intent, cold look.
battle: On the seventh night of the ball, beside the silver dish: the faded red robe under a dark red stole, the sleeves tied back. He holds a slip of paper written in blood in one hand and a thin bone stylus in the other; he carries no weapon.
battle_pose: 3) the rite outfit: tense and intent, the feet set, a cold, focused expression, a slip of blood-written paper held up in one hand and a thin bone stylus in the other; he carries no weapon.
formal: In full vestments at the long table: the faded red robe under a long dark red stole edged with tarnished silver, a small silver bowl held in both hands. He stands very upright, a serene, unblinking look.
art: A portrait with the camera tilted, the face large, the vermilion eyes looking at the viewer over a courteous smile that does not reach them, a dark-red fingertip raised as if to write. Warm candlelight from one side in a dark ballroom, red light pooling on a silver dish. Foreground blur: candle flames, drifting rose petals and the rim of a silver dish.

name: 维吉莉亚
src: 山铜纪/山铜纪时段_五_七城的年月.md:4007
who: Vigilia, a demon-kin of the bone folk, of the family that keeps the oldest bell tower of the grave city of bells, and its bell-tower keeper; eight hundred and forty-two in 779, visibly old, looking about seventy-five: small, about 150 cm, the back a little bent, though she sits upright. Her bones show at the surface: the cheekbones, the jaw and all ten knuckles are bare white bone, smooth as old ivory. On her forehead bone a small carved mark, her number, with a row of twelve notches beside it worn almost flat. Thin white hair in a tight small knot. Greyish-white eyes that peer close at everything. A slow, terse air; she gives you a number before she asks your name.
face: FACE, as in the references: an old bone-folk woman's face, visibly old, small and narrow, NOT young: the cheekbones and jaw are bare smooth white bone at the surface with pale thin skin between; a small carved mark and a row of worn notches on the forehead bone; greyish-white eyes, a little filmy, narrowed to peer close; deep lines at the eyes and mouth; a thin, patient mouth. Skin shadows a soft cool grey.
build: about 150 cm, small and thin, the back a little bent.
palette: bell-tower grey and bone white, faded slate, a little old bronze
casual: The bell-tower keeper's dress: a long grey robe with a high collar buttoned to the throat, a small bell embroidered at the hem, the sleeves tied back with cord for the bell rope, soft shoes; a carved bone tag on a cord at her chest. She holds a handful of bone tags, feeling them with her eyes half closed.
private: By the low stool under the bell tower where she teaches the grave city's children their numbers: a plain grey wool robe with no bell on it, a dark grey shawl, the bone tag on its cord. She holds out one bone tag between two white-boned fingers. A dry, patient look.
battle: The thirteen nights in the deepest archive under the tower: the high-collared grey robe, the sleeves tied back, a small lamp hung at her belt. She holds a mouldering old name-register open close to her face and reads it with her bare-boned fingertips; she does not fight.
battle_pose: 3) the archive outfit: tense and intent, the feet set, a firm expression, an old name-register held open close to her face, the bare-boned fingertips of one hand tracing its page; she does not fight.
formal: On the night the oldest bell was given its name: the high-collared grey robe with the bell at its hem under a long dark grey hooded mantle, the bone tag polished. She stands very straight with the hands folded in front, a grave, still look.
art: A portrait with the camera tilted, the face large, the greyish-white eyes half closed as she listens, a bare-boned finger raised to the worn notches on her forehead. Cold grey light from a bell-tower window on one side, a faint bronze glow from a great bell above. Foreground blur: a thick bell rope, hanging bone tags and drifting dust. She wears the high-collared grey robe.

name: 巴尔缇娜·格雷恩
src: 山铜纪/山铜纪时段_五_七城的年月.md:4026
who: Baltina Grayne, the Grey Witch, a long-lived demon-kin found as a baby in the last basket in the rain city's south gate, who leads the outcasts of the west from camp to camp and writes every name in her book; about eight hundred and fifty, growing again since the night by the dark river, now a grown woman who looks twenty-five or twenty-six: about 168 cm, slender, long-legged and high-waisted. Long straight ash-silver hair, darker grey toward the tips, worn loose. Gold eyes that glow at night like molten mountain copper. A small ruby-like mark at one temple. Cold pale skin. Short pointed ears. A calm, terse, watchful air; she asks your name first and says she will write it down.
build: 168 cm, slender, long-legged and high-waisted.
palette: ash silver and road grey, black leather, mountain-copper bronze, one small ember red
casual: Her road clothes in the western camps: a long deep grey coat with buttons of mountain copper, its hem always stained with the dust of somewhere else, over a plain dark long-sleeved dress of the western cut; a black leather glove on the right hand reaching to the elbow and a short black glove on the left; a leather-bound notebook hanging at her belt on a cord; a plain short-barrelled gun of her own making tucked at the back of the belt. She holds a pen of grey ink, about to write a name, a calm, attentive look.
private: In her grey tent at the heart of the great camp: a soft long grey wool dress with a high neck and long sleeves, the gloves off, the hair loose over one shoulder. She holds a heel of bread, the same ration as everyone in the camp. A tired, quiet, almost gentle look.
battle: Riding in after a disaster to count who came back: a grey hooded travelling cloak over the long deep grey coat, the gloves on, riding boots, the notebook at her belt. She holds low in one hand the plain short-barrelled black-powder gun she made herself, no runes cut on it, pointed at the ground; a still, cold, level look.
formal: Seated as a guest at a great feast she was invited to: the long deep grey coat brushed and buttoned over a long black dress with a high collar, the black gloves, the ash-silver hair loose with no ornament. She stands very upright, the hands folded, a serene, distant look.
art: A portrait with the camera tilted, the face large, the gold eyes looking at the viewer calmly as if asking your name, one black-gloved hand holding an open notebook near her collar. Cold grey dawn light over a camp from one side, a faint ember glow from a campfire on the other. Foreground blur: falling grey ash, drifting embers and the edge of a blank page.

name: 西比拉
src: 山铜纪/山铜纪时段_五_七城的年月.md:4104
who: Sibylla, a demon-kin of the nightmare bloodline, a dream-charmer, head of the Mirror Hall house that keeps the great name mirror of the mirror city, elder sister of the dream-warden; two hundred and five in 803 and looking about fifty: about 165 cm, straight-backed and spare. Deep violet hair going grey, wound up in a tight, severe knot. Dark violet eyes, the dream-reading eyes of her house. A composed, cool face with fine lines. Every morning she wipes the great name mirror with a soft cloth. A terse, commanding air; she speaks of the hall and never of herself.
face: FACE, as in the references: a severe, composed woman's face of about fifty, NOT young: fine lines at the eyes and beside the mouth; medium, narrow almond eyes of dark violet; thin straight brows; a firm, closed mouth. Pale clean skin with very little shading; skin shadows a soft cool lilac.
build: about 165 cm, straight-backed and spare.
palette: deep teal and dark violet, mist grey, black lake, a little dull silver
casual: The Mirror Hall's dress: a long deep teal robe with the cuffs and collar fitted close, a dark grey sash, soft dark shoes, nothing on her that reflects; a folded soft cloth tucked in the sash for wiping the mirror. She holds the cloth in one hand, the other at her waist, a cool, watchful look.
private: In the family rooms of the hall late at night: a soft dark grey wool dress with a high collar, a knitted violet shawl, the knot a little loosened. She holds a sealed letter she has not yet sent. A tired, guarded look.
battle: Through the seven days the city lay drowned in dreams: the teal robe belted tight, the sleeves tied back. She holds an oil can in one hand and a small lamp in the other, keeping the lamps by the sleepers lit; she does not fight.
battle_pose: 3) the night-watch outfit: tense and upright, the feet set, a firm expression, an oil can held in one hand and a small lamp in the other; she does not fight.
formal: As head of the Mirror Hall before the name mirror: a long deep teal robe with a high close collar under a long dark violet mantle, the hair in its tight knot, nothing on her that reflects. She stands very upright with the hands folded in front, a severe, composed look.
art: A portrait with the camera tilted, the face large, the dark violet eyes looking at the viewer coolly over a soft cloth she holds raised as if about to wipe a mirror. Cold silver mist light from one side over a black lake. Foreground blur: drifting mist, faint glimmers of reflected light and the dark edge of a great mirror.

name: 赫丝珀
src: 山铜纪/山铜纪时段_五_七城的年月.md:4124
who: Hesper, a demon-kin night-wing, eldest of the oldest High-Nest families, who live in the old observatory under the sealed lamp room at the top of the leaning sky tower; three hundred and forty-four in 824 and looking about seventy: about 166 cm, thin, her back still straight. A pair of feathered night-wings folded down her back, dusky blue-grey with the feathers half gone white. Thin silver-white hair braided and wound round her head. Pale amber eyes. A long, lined face. A slow, gentle, unyielding air; she speaks to everyone as to a child of her house.
face: FACE, as in the references: an old night-wing woman's face of about seventy, long and lined, NOT young: deep lines at the eyes and mouth; narrow pale amber eyes, calm and kind; thin white brows; a gentle but firm mouth. Pale clean skin with very little shading; skin shadows a soft cool tone.
build: about 166 cm, thin and upright.
palette: dusky blue-grey and silver-white, pale amber, old parchment, a little lamp gold
casual: The dress of the tower's old families: a long dusky blue wool robe with two slits in the back for the wings, the cuffs tied with thin cord, a pale grey shawl, soft felt shoes. She holds a rolled old star chart in both hands, a calm, gentle look.
private: Sitting watch under the lamp-room door at night: a thick grey knitted shawl over the long robe, the wings folded. She holds a small cup of warm tea. A peaceful, faraway look.
battle: The night the tower falls and she will not come down: the blue robe, the grey shawl pinned tight, the wings folded close. She stands with both hands resting on the rolled star chart, refusing to move; she does not fight.
battle_pose: 3) the last-night outfit: still and unmoving, the feet set, a calm, resolute expression, both hands resting on a rolled star chart held before her; she does not fight.
formal: As eldest of the High-Nest families: a long dusky blue robe embroidered at the hem with small stars, a long pale grey mantle, a thin silver chain across the brow, the wings folded neatly. She stands very straight with the hands folded, a serene, proud look.
art: A portrait with the camera tilted, the face large, the pale amber eyes looking at the viewer kindly and immovably, a half-white wing sweeping past her shoulder. Warm gold light leaking from under a closed door on one side against a cold night sky. Foreground blur: old star-chart parchment, drifting white feathers and a thin line of light.

name: 法伊勒·枷匠
src: 山铜纪/山铜纪时段_五_七城的年月.md:4138
who: Feyle Shacklewright, a demon-kin troll of the Thunder-Gaol folk, daughter of the head of the shackle-making family, who has led the wasteland folk in the thunder vault for over a hundred years; about a hundred and eighty in 847 and looking just past fifty: very tall, about 225 cm, big-boned. Thick hide of grey with a blue-green tint. Her head is shaved completely bare, as no one under the thunder keeps hair. Pale gold eyes under a heavy brow. Under the skin of both hands glows a purple-copper light, brighter than her son's; when she opens her hands, purple sparks crackle in her palms. On a leather cord at her neck hangs an old branding-iron head from the seventh pit, her father's, its mark worn smooth. A cold, sparing, iron air.
face: FACE, as in the references: a broad, heavy-boned troll woman's face of about fifty, NOT young: deep-set pale gold eyes under a heavy brow, hard lines at their corners; a wide flat nose; a set, unsmiling mouth. Thick grey hide with a blue-green tint and very little shading; skin shadows a soft cool slate.
build: about 225 cm, very tall and big-boned, with broad shoulders and long strong arms.
palette: slate grey with blue-green, thunder purple, purple-copper glow, grey wolf fur, iron black
casual: The dress of the wasteland folk: a long coat sewn from thunder-maned wolf pelts, grey fur outward, worn against the lightning, over a coarse dark tunic and wrapped leggings, hide boots; the branding-iron head on its cord at her neck. Her hands hang at her sides with the purple light glowing under the skin, a cold, steady look.
private: Deep in the thunder vault: a coarse undyed long-sleeved tunic, the wolf-pelt coat off, the branding-iron on its cord. She holds a bowl of pale cave mushrooms. A hard, tired look.
battle: Leading her people out of the vault onto the great round dais: the thunder-wolf pelt coat belted, leather wraps on the forearms, the iron head on its cord. One hand is raised to shoulder height with purple sparks crackling in the open palm, the other clenched; she carries no weapon.
battle_pose: 3) the storm outfit: tense and commanding, the feet planted wide, a hard expression, one hand raised to shoulder height with purple sparks crackling in the open palm and the other hand clenched; she carries no weapon.
formal: On a night of the thunder rite: a long cloak of thunder-wolf pelt with a stiff high collar over a dark tunic, bone beads at the wrists, the branding-iron head on its cord. She stands very upright with the hands folded, a stern, fervent look.
art: A portrait with the camera tilted, the face large, the pale gold eyes looking at the viewer without mercy, purple sparks crackling in a raised palm. Violet-white lightning light from one side, a pillar of thunder far behind. Foreground blur: crackling sparks, a swinging branding-iron head and drifting grit.

name: 达丽
src: 山铜纪/山铜纪时段_五_七城的年月.md:4160
who: Dari of the First Pit Camp, a demon-kin of the bull-horned Thunder-Gaol folk who digs mountain copper in the mining belt, whose daughter was carried off into the storm wasteland; fifty-seven in 847 and looking thirty-five or thirty-six: short, about 158 cm, sturdy, with thick shoulders. Deep bronze-coloured skin. A pair of short horns worn smooth and shiny. Short ash-lilac hair. Copper-gold eyes. Hands hard with a miner's calluses; after the march, a mark round her left wrist where a short chain was locked. A plain, terse, unbending air; she speaks only of what has to be done next.
build: about 158 cm, short and sturdy, with thick shoulders and strong arms.
palette: deep bronze and ash lilac, copper gold, canvas brown, a little dull iron
casual: Her miner's clothes: canvas work clothes with leather patches on the knees and elbows, a short coarse jacket over a dark shirt, a wide leather belt, heavy boots; a small hand pick at her belt. She stands with the arms at her sides, a hard, unreadable look.
private: At home in the First Pit Camp: a long brown wool dress with long sleeves, a knitted shawl, soft boots. She holds a small wooden comb, about to comb her daughter's tangled hair. A rare, softer look.
battle: Locked to the end of the chain beside the condemned: the canvas work clothes belted tight, leather wraps on the forearms, a short length of iron chain locked to her left wrist. She grips a short mining pick in her right hand, a fierce, set look.
formal: At the memorial stone on the anniversary of the march: a clean dark wool coat buttoned to the collar over a long dark skirt, the horns polished. She stands very straight with the hands at her sides, a grave, unforgiving look.
art: A portrait with the camera tilted, the face large, the copper-gold eyes looking straight at the viewer, hard and unwavering, the chain mark showing on the wrist of a raised hand. Violet storm light from one side. Foreground blur: links of iron chain, drifting grit and a small hand pick.

name: 蓓雅
src: 山铜纪/山铜纪时段_五_七城的年月.md:4161
who: Bea, Dari's daughter, a demon-kin girl of the bull-horned Thunder-Gaol folk from the First Pit Camp of the mining belt, eight years old in 847 and looking exactly eight, a small child and NOT a teenager: about 118 cm, wholly covered by her clothes. Messy ash-lilac hair with two little horn buds just poking through it. Copper-gold eyes like her mother's. Deep bronze-coloured skin. She asks things straight out and takes every word literally. A curious, plain-spoken, brave little air.
palette: ash lilac and copper gold, deep bronze, oatmeal wool, a little faded red
casual: Her everyday clothes in the mining camp: a long-sleeved oatmeal wool tunic to the knees over thick wool leggings, a small brown wool jacket a size too big, sturdy little boots. She holds a small smooth stone she found, a curious, wide-eyed look.
private: At home at bedtime: a long soft cream nightdress with long sleeves and a high round neck, a knitted shawl, thick socks. She holds a cup of warm milk in both hands. A sleepy look.
battle: On the long walk home through the wasteland: the brown jacket buttoned up over the wool tunic, a grey wool hood, the boots wrapped with cloth. She clutches a folded grey blanket to her chest; she does not fight.
battle_pose: 3) the march outfit: wary and brave, the feet a little apart, a determined little frown, a folded grey blanket clutched to her chest in both arms; she does not fight.
formal: The day she goes with her mother to the memorial stone: a clean long-sleeved dark blue wool dress to the shins with a small white collar, the messy hair combed and tied with a red ribbon, sturdy boots. She stands very straight with the hands clasped in front, a solemn little face.
art: A head-and-shoulders portrait, the face turned slightly, the copper-gold eyes looking at the viewer with a wide, wondering stare, as if she has just seen lightning lie down on someone. Violet-white dawn light after a storm from one side. Foreground blur: faint drifting sparks of purple light and a strand of messy ash-lilac hair. She wears the brown wool jacket buttoned to the collar.
